archetypes.name: stale-ref-sweep
archetypes.rationale: The plan mandates a completeness grep for the retired argv token but lists only 13 specific files to modify; unlisted files (other skill docs, agent prompts, alias definitions, flag-signature lint scripts) may harbor stale references that would fail the plan's own completeness gate.
archetypes.prompt_body: Grep for the retired `--simple` argv token across all *.md, *.sh, *.json, *.txt, *.tsv, and *.toml files in the repository, excluding larch-logs/**, .git/, and CHANGELOG.md, and cross-reference every hit against the plan's explicit file list. Identify any files that contain the retired token but are absent from the plan's 'Files to modify' section — these are unplanned edit sites the completeness gate would catch at runtime. Also check whether the token appears in alias definitions, argument-hint lint patterns, flag-signature lint scripts, or agent prompt files that the plan does not mention. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: test-needle-fidelity
archetypes.rationale: The plan prescribes specific grep-needle changes to three test harnesses; if a described 'before' needle does not match the actual current test-file content, the change description is wrong and the CI failure will differ from or precede what the plan predicts.
archetypes.prompt_body: For each test-file edit described in the plan — scripts/test-design-structure.sh, skills/design/scripts/test-design-driver.sh, and skills/design/scripts/test-render-final-summary.sh — read the current file and confirm that each needle or assertion the plan expects to remove is present with exactly the described text or structure. Verify whether the existing assertions for the retired tier gate and its outcome use exact string literals or variable-backed patterns that diverge from the plan's description. Check that the plan's proposed replacement needles (default-SIMPLE tier resolution prose, disallowed-flag rejection prose, surviving early-cancel outcome swap) correspond to prose that will plausibly exist in the target skill files after the described edits are applied. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
